about: Cells: what a session's door says to a piece of PACT Core handed in during a run (docs/100 §4.5, §6). Replayed as `Session.cell(cell, by=by, takes=takes, gives=gives)` on a session opened on `tree`; each case is decided on its own, and an admitted cell is ended before the next. `by` is the agent of the workspace that wrote the cell: the cell may call what that agent was given (each action of each tool it `uses:`, and its teammates) and what the cell itself defines. `cell` is the text: any helper blocks first, then the statements to carry out. The session wraps the statements as a flow that takes `takes` and gives `gives`. In `expect`: `admitted`; `refused-by` is the door that refused it, `checker` when `pact check` did (then `rule` is the checker's rule) and otherwise the session guard by name: `floor` (a cell may define agents, flows, shapes and actors and nothing of the workspace's own, and must have statements), `meter` (a cell has a most size, length, number of blocks and depth, decided before it is read), `collision` (a cell never replaces what the workspace has), `reach` (it calls something its writer was not given) and `wider` (a helper it defines uses a tool, writes a setting or may take more steps than its writer). `defines` is what the session had more of while the cell lived. A runtime's own wording for a guard's refusal is its own; which door refuses, and which rule of the checker, is what is held.
